newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria hit by petrol shortages.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria hit by petrol shortages.

text.p: Bulgaria is suffering petrol and diesel shortages as suppliers hold back product in the expectation of further price rises, energy officials said on Monday.

The officials, who asked not to be identified, said the country's biggest oil refinery Neftohim and firms buying petrol from it were keeping petrol in storage in order to sell after prices were raised.
Many filling stations owned by the country's biggest gasoline distributor Petrol in Bulgaria's second city Plovdiv said they had run out of gasoline and were closed on Monday.
Around the country, only a handful of Petrol filling stations had all gasoline types as well as diesel.
Shell Bulgaria AD, a unit of Royal Dutch/Shell Group, said its petrol stations faced problems in fuel supplies from Neftohim and could not offer a full range of products.
"Supplies are disrupted and we have no official information from the Neftohim refinery," Shell spokeswoman Yulita Decheva said.
The government usually revises energy prices each month in line with inflation, the exchange rate and world oil prices.
On Thursday, the cabinet raised petrol and diesel prices for the second time in as many weeks after the lev fell sharply against the dollar.

Petrol's executive director Bedo Doganyan denied that his firm had been withholding petrol in expectation of price rises. "We have petrol at our storages although they are not full up," Doganyan told Reuters.
Petrol has 450 filling stations in the country and supplies a third of the fuel market, Doganyan said.
The Neftohim refinery declined comment on the petrol shortages and the volumes of its daily deliveries.
Spokeswoman Tatyana Hadzhieva said the plant had been refining 18,000 tonnes of crude per day. The plant's daily volumes were about 22,000 tonnes during the summer.
However, refinery officials said the reason for the shortages could not be a lack of crude as the plant had enough "for the time being".
Local newspapers said Neftohim's board had held an emergency meeting on Sunday and would ask the government this week to approve a new petrol price rise of 34.6 percent.
They said the refinery would reduce the volume of Russian crude it was buying as the plant owed million of dollars to some of its crude suppliers.
From last Friday, petrol costs 141-186 levs per litre while diesel costs 112 levs.
